newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - AUGUST 14.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - AUGUST 14.

text.p: HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - The main impulse for the recent increase in petrol and diesel prices, scheduled by Benzina a.s. to take place today is a recent rise in the distributor's price by refiner Ceska Rafinerska a.s., according to Jaroslav Ruzek from Ceska Rafinerska.

- The government is willing to offer Intel incentives if the firm agrees to build a plant to manufacture and test microprocessors in the Czech Republic, according to the Minister of Trade and Industry Karel Kuhnl.

- Motokov International will obtain 34 percent of the largest domestic tractor manufacturer, Zetor. The government approved the direct sale of the shares, which will be from those currently held by Konsolidacni Banka, according to the Minister of Trade and Industry, Karel Kuhnl.

- Czech Railways is planning to increase passenger fares from September 1, according to general manager, Vladimir Sosna. Fares will increase by 50 percent on short routes and from 20 to 30 percent on longer routes.
- The crown is weaker against the mark on the interbank market, though stronger against the dollar according to Petr Korous from Ceskoslovenska Obchodni Banka.

- Kaucuk Kralupy posted a gross profit of 144 million crowns on turnover of almost three billion crowns in the first half of 1997, according to Kaucuk's financial director, Vladimir Linda. This is some 300 million crowns lower over the same period last year on roughly equivalent turnover.

- Skoda Ostrov, one of the largest trolleybus manufacturers in the world, will provide 117 trolleybuses to a number of Russian cities, according to Skoda spokesman Karel Samec. PRAVO - The government will provide 500 million crowns from the state budget for the construction of new housing in regions recently hit by heavy flooding, according to Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus. A region will receive approximately 500,000 crowns for the construction of each apartment. MLADA FRONTA DNES - Increases in the price of petrol and diesel fuel will likely also be evident in higher prices for shipping firms, according to the general secretary of Cesmad Bohemia, an association of domestic shipping companies.
